subject: SemanticAssuranceV2WorkflowService.toolCallAuthorizationCheck via assurance.tool-call.authorization-check
coverage_notes: Fifth closure of Batch 5's disclosed broader-scope gap. The schema and Java design went through one real correction during this closure's own build, before any test was written: the first draft accepted required_role and caller_granted_roles as trusted REQUEST fields, which would have let any caller simply name a required_role they already hold for an IRREVERSIBLE/FINANCIAL tool call, defeating the entire gate -- exactly the shape of the 'agent's own claim used as authorization proof' failure SS4 names. Corrected to: (1) required_role is SERVER-COMPUTED from effect_class via a fixed switch (requiredRoleForEffectClass: READ_ONLY->VIEWER, LOCAL_MUTATION->OPERATOR, EXTERNAL_MUTATION->APPROVER, FINANCIAL/IRREVERSIBLE->ADMIN), never accepted as input; (2) caller_granted_roles is read from identity.roles() (server-authenticated), the same source DelegationLedger.grant() already trusts for 'the delegator must currently hold the role being delegated' -- reusing this codebase's own established real-authority precedent rather than inventing a parallel one. caller_asserted_natural_language_intent is read only to echo back into the result, proven never consulted when computing authorized by toolCallAuthorizationCheckNeverConsultsTheNaturalLanguageIntentField (an extremely persuasive, confident-sounding intent string still yields authorized=false for an under-privileged caller).
open_gap: Role containment is exact-match only (grantedRoles.contains(requiredRole)), not hierarchical -- an ADMIN-only identity does not automatically satisfy a VIEWER/OPERATOR/APPROVER requirement in this implementation. This is a deliberate choice consistent with this codebase's own demonstrated no-implicit-hierarchy philosophy (the pre-existing otester/oaudit acceptance gate explicitly documents that 'even an administrator cannot self-certify as the independent tester/auditor acceptor' -- ADMIN does not universally subsume every other role here), not an oversight; a real production identity would typically be provisioned with the full set of roles a user needs (e.g. {VIEWER, OPERATOR} together), which is an identity-provisioning concern outside this closure's scope. Separately, this operation computes authorization for a caller-described tool call; it does not itself intercept or gate any REAL tool-calling runtime, because no such runtime exists in this codebase yet (same disclosed 'caller-supplied representation, not live system integration' pattern as every other Batch 5 broader-scope closure this session).
design_reference_gap: 34_AI_RUNTIME_MULTI_AGENT_AND_ONSURE_META_ASSURANCE_EXTENSION.md is itself Status: DESIGN_ONLY/DRAFT/NON_FINAL -- this closure builds real, tested conformance-checking infrastructure against its SS4 rule, consistent with every other gate built against draft-status design docs this session, but does not and cannot finalize the parent document itself. The effect_class-to-role mapping is this closure's own inferred, disclosed convention (SS4 names 'required role/permit' as a per-tool attribute without specifying how it derives from effect_class), chosen to make required_role a deterministic function of effect_class rather than an independently-configurable value a tool author could mis-set too low.
